setlist_extra.title: Stuck Inside Mobile with the Memphis Blues Again

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **feel like a stranger** (1 review): Brent's synth was out of action early in Stranger, which was otherwise stringy and cool; Jerry's voice was rough [23]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Franklin's Tower had eager basslines but was otherwise a standard version [23]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Minglewood in the first set is singled out as a standout, with a very tight set overall [16]
- **Memphis Blues** (1 review): Listener calls this the best Memphis Blues they have heard, live or on tape [24]
- **big railroad blues** (1 review): Big Railroad Blues is described as a fairly uncommon song to hear [22]
- **around and around** (1 review): Around and Around closed the first set [22]
- **sugar magnolia** (1 review): The second-set run of Sugar Magnolia into Scarlet Begonias, Estimated Prophet and Eyes of the World is highlighted [16]
- **the wheel** (1 review): During The Wheel, fans way up in the rafters circled the arena [26]

## Setlist highlights

- **radio jabber**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **radio intro :23**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [28]
- **radio outro :26**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-04-07.127683.FM.flac16** (recommended): FM broadcast; 23 songs; 149 min [1]
- **gd1988-04-07.sbd.miller.91163.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 140 min; rated 4.12/5 by 8 [4]
- **gd1988-04-07.156054.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 140 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1988-04-07.156450.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: soundboard; 20 songs; 140 min [8]
- **gd88-04-07.pre-fm.hinko.17684.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 20 songs; 141 min; rated 4.08/5 by 12 [11]. Said about its sound: Sound is very good but not perfect; Recording has a radio signal or interference cutting in now and then; Generally very good recording, but with radio fuzz at the starts of songs, as on FM broadcast tapes [17][18][27]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: radio [1]
- Listener attended and remembers it rocking; first time hearing it again since the show [18]
- Listener was in the fifth row; says Jerry, Bobby and Phil were all playing well [19]
- Worcester parking lot was cold, rainy, and unpleasant, with police arresting many people [22]
- It was the listener's first Dead show, and they danced all night [24]
- Jerry was battling a cold, so his vocals were imperfect [27]
- Listener considers it the best of the spring 1988 shows they have heard [17]
- Part of a three-night run; Jerry's voice was recovering and his playing solid. The 4-9-88 Rosemont show is also liked [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-04-07.127683.FM.flac16**: source: WCUW Worcester 91.3 FM stereo broadcast > reciever > Teac 3340 reel recorder (3.3/4 ips) > Maxell UD 7" master reel > (1st set copied to 1g reel) > played on… [1]
- **gd1988-04-07.sbd.miller.91163.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) D [4]. Also: Stuck Inside of Mobile is patched from an FM source, via unknown, VHS, DAT and CD, with pitch correction [4]
- **gd1988-04-07.156054.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  March 10, 2022; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90) [5]
- **gd1988-04-07.156450.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  March 10, 2022; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90) [8]. Also: Ultramatrix recording by Don Pearson and Dan Healy, combining multiple masters; this copy is converted from 24-bit/96k to 16-bit/44.1k [8]
- **gd88-04-07.pre-fm.hinko.17684.sbeok.shnf**: source: Pre-FM > MR > VHS > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN (seekable) Via Darryl Hinko [11]
